sanskrit: surathaṃ tu tataḥ kruddham āpatantaṃ mahāratham cukopa samare drauṇir daṇḍāhata ivoragaḥ
english: Then, as the wrathful Suratha, that mighty car-warrior, came rushing upon him, the son of Droṇa blazed with rage in the battle, like a serpent struck with a staff.

sanskrit: triśikhāṃ bhrukuṭīṃ kṛtvā sṛkkiṇī parilelihan udvīkṣya surathaṃ roṣād dhanurjyām avamṛjya ca mumoca tīkṣṇaṃ nārācaṃ yamadaṇḍasamadyutim
english: Knitting his brow into a triple furrow and licking the corners of his mouth, glaring at Suratha in his fury and drawing back his bowstring, he loosed a keen iron shaft that shone like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: sa tasya hṛdayaṃ bhittvā praviveśātivegataḥ śakrāśanir ivotsṛṣṭā vidārya dharaṇītalam
english: Cleaving through his heart, it sank in with tremendous speed, like the thunderbolt of Śakra hurled down to rend the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ patitaṃ bhūmau nārācena samāhatam vajreṇeva yathā śṛṅgaṃ parvatasya mahādhanam
english: Then he fell to the ground, smitten by that iron shaft, like the precious peak of a mountain struck down by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ tam eva rathināṃ varaḥ
english: When that hero had been slain, the valiant son of Droṇa, foremost of car-warriors, swiftly mounted that very chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ sajjo mahārāja drauṇir āhavadurmadaḥ arjunaṃ yodhayām āsa saṃśaptakavṛto raṇe
english: Then, made ready, O great king, the son of Droṇa, frenzied in battle, fought against Arjuna, surrounded by the saṃśaptakas in the fray.

sanskrit: tatra yuddhaṃ mahac cāsīd arjunasya paraiḥ saha madhyaṃdinagate sūrye yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: There a great battle was fought between Arjuna and his foes, while the sun stood at midday—a battle that swelled the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tatrāścaryam apaśyāma dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ parākramam yad eko yugapad vīrān samayodhayad arjunaḥ
english: There we beheld a marvel, witnessing their prowess: that Arjuna alone fought against those heroes all at once.

sanskrit: vimardas tu mahān āsīd arjunasya paraiḥ saha śatakrator yathā pūrvaṃ mahatyā daityasenayā
english: And great was the clash between Arjuna and his foes, as of old between Śatakratu and the vast host of the Daityas.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca duryodhano mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ cakratuḥ sumahad yuddhaṃ śaraśaktisamākulam
english: Saṃjaya said: Duryodhana, O great king, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata waged a tremendous battle, thick with arrows and spears.

sanskrit: tayor āsan mahārāja śaradhārāḥ sahasraśaḥ ambudānāṃ yathā kāle jaladhārāḥ samantataḥ
english: Between the two, O great king, the streams of arrows flowed by thousands on every side, as the showers of rain from the clouds in their season.

sanskrit: rājā tu pārṣataṃ viddhvā śaraiḥ pañcabhir āyasaiḥ droṇahantāram ugreṣuḥ punar vivyādha saptabhiḥ
english: The king, piercing the son of Pṛṣata, the slayer of Droṇa, with five iron arrows, that fierce archer then struck him again with seven.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu samare balavān dṛḍhavikramaḥ saptatyā viśikhānāṃ vai duryodhanam apīḍayat
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, mighty and firm in valor, sorely afflicted Duryodhana in battle with seventy shafts.

sanskrit: pīḍitaṃ prekṣya rājānaṃ sodaryā bharatarṣabha mahatyā senayā sārdhaṃ parivavruḥ sma pārṣatam
english: Seeing the king hard pressed, his own brothers, O bull of the Bhāratas, together with a great host surrounded the son of Pṛṣata.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ śūraiḥ sarvato 'tirathair bhṛśam vyacarat samare rājan darśayan hastalāghavam
english: Hemmed in on all sides by those heroes, those mighty car-warriors, he ranged through the battle, O king, displaying the lightness of his hand.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī kṛtavarmāṇaṃ gautamaṃ ca mahāratham prabhadrakaiḥ samāyukto yodhayām āsa dhanvinau
english: Śikhaṇḍin, joined by the Prabhadrakas, fought against Kṛtavarman and the descendant of Gotama, that mighty car-warrior—both of them archers.

sanskrit: tatrāpi sumahad yuddhaṃ ghorarūpaṃ viśāṃ pate prāṇān saṃtyajatāṃ yuddhe prāṇadyūtābhidevane
english: There too, O lord of the people, a tremendous and terrible battle was fought by men casting away their lives, as in a gambling-match with life itself for the stake.

sanskrit: śalyas tu śaravarṣāṇi vimuñcan sarvatodiśam pāṇḍavān pīḍayām āsa sasātyakivṛkodarān
english: And Śalya, loosing showers of arrows in every direction, sorely pressed the Pāṇḍavas, together with Sātyaki and Vṛkodara.

sanskrit: tathobhau ca yamau yuddhe yamatulyaparākramau yodhayām āsa rājendra vīryeṇa ca balena ca
english: And the two twins as well, whose prowess equalled Yama's, he fought in battle, O lord of kings, with valor and with might.

sanskrit: śalyasāyakanunnānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahāmṛdhe trātāraṃ nādhyagacchanta ke cit tatra mahārathāḥ
english: For the Pāṇḍavas, driven back by Śalya's arrows in that great fray, certain of their mighty car-warriors could find no protector there.

sanskrit: tatas tu nakulaḥ śūro dharmarāje prapīḍite abhidudrāva vegena mātulaṃ mādrinandanaḥ
english: Then the heroic Nakula, the son of Mādrī, when the King of Righteousness was hard pressed, rushed with speed against his maternal uncle.

sanskrit: saṃchādya samare śalyaṃ nakulaḥ paravīrahā vivyādha cainaṃ daśabhiḥ smayamānaḥ stanāntare
english: Veiling Śalya in battle, Nakula, slayer of hostile heroes, smiling as he did so, pierced him with ten shafts in the breast.

sanskrit: sarvapāraśavair bāṇaiḥ karmāraparimārjitaiḥ svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilādhautair dhanuryantrapracoditaiḥ
english: They were arrows all of iron, burnished by the smith, golden-feathered, whetted on stone, sped by the engine of his bow.

sanskrit: śalyas tu pīḍitas tena svasrīyeṇa mahātmanā nakulaṃ pīḍayām āsa patribhir nataparvabhiḥ
english: But Śalya, sorely pressed by that high-souled son of his sister, in turn afflicted Nakula with feathered shafts smoothed at the joints.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhīmaseno 'tha sātyakiḥ sahadevaś ca mādreyo madrarājam upādravan
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, and Bhīmasena, and Sātyaki, and Sahadeva the son of Mādrī rushed upon the King of the Madras.

sanskrit: tān āpatata evāśu pūrayānān rathasvanaiḥ diśaś ca pradiśaś caiva kampayānāṃś ca medinīm pratijagrāha samare senāpatir amitrajit
english: As they came swiftly on, filling the quarters and the intermediate quarters with the rattle of their chariots and making the earth tremble, the commander, conqueror of his foes, received them in battle.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tribhir viddhvā bhīmasenaṃ ca saptabhiḥ sātyakiṃ ca śatenājau sahadevaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Piercing Yudhiṣṭhira with three shafts, and Bhīmasena with seven, and Sātyaki with a hundred in the fight, and Sahadeva with three arrows—

sanskrit: tatas tu saśaraṃ cāpaṃ nakulasya mahātmanaḥ madreśvaraḥ kṣurapreṇa tadā ciccheda māriṣa tad aśīryata vicchinnaṃ dhanuḥ śalyasya sāyakaiḥ
english: Then the lord of the Madras, with a razor-edged arrow, cut through the bow of the high-souled Nakula together with the shaft set to it, O sire; and so, severed by Śalya's arrows, that bow fell to pieces.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya mādrīputro mahārathaḥ madrarājarathaṃ tūrṇaṃ pūrayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Then, taking up another bow, the son of Mādrī, that mighty car-warrior, swiftly covered the chariot of the Madra king with feathered shafts.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu madreśaṃ sahadevaś ca māriṣa daśabhir daśabhir bāṇair urasy enam avidhyatām
english: And Yudhiṣṭhira and Sahadeva, O sire, each pierced the lord of the Madras in the breast with ten arrows apiece.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tataḥ ṣaṣṭyā sātyakir navabhiḥ śaraiḥ madrarājam abhidrutya jaghnatuḥ kaṅkapatribhiḥ
english: Then Bhīmasena with sixty and Sātyaki with nine arrows, rushing upon the Madra king, struck him with heron-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: madrarājas tataḥ kruddhaḥ sātyakiṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha bhūyaḥ saptatyā śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām
english: Then the Madra king in wrath pierced Sātyaki with nine arrows, and again with seventy shafts smoothed at the joints.

sanskrit: athāsya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ muṣṭau ciccheda māriṣa hayāṃś ca caturaḥ saṃkhye preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: Then he cut through his bow, shaft and all, at the grip, O sire, and dispatched his four horses to death in the encounter.

sanskrit: virathaṃ sātyakiṃ kṛtvā madrarājo mahābalaḥ viśikhānāṃ śatenainam ājaghāna samantataḥ
english: Having made Sātyaki carless, the mighty Madra king smote him on every side with a hundred shafts.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau tu saṃrabdhau bhīmasenaṃ ca pāṇḍavam yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca kauravya vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And the two enraged sons of Mādrī, and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, and Yudhiṣṭhira, O Kaurava, he pierced each with ten arrows.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma madrarājasya pauruṣam yad enaṃ sahitāḥ pārthā nābhyavartanta saṃyuge
english: There we beheld the wondrous manhood of the Madra king, in that the sons of Pṛthā, even united, could not overcome him in the encounter.

sanskrit: athānyaṃ ratham āsthāya sātyakiḥ satyavikramaḥ pīḍitān pāṇḍavān dṛṣṭvā madrarājavaśaṃ gatān abhidudrāva vegena madrāṇām adhipaṃ balī
english: Then, mounting another chariot, Sātyaki of true valor, seeing the Pāṇḍavas hard pressed and fallen into the power of the Madra king, rushed with speed, mighty as he was, upon the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: āpatantaṃ rathaṃ tasya śalyaḥ samitiśobhanaḥ pratyudyayau rathenaiva matto mattam iva dvipam
english: As his chariot came rushing on, Śalya, the splendor of assemblies, advanced against it with his own chariot, as one furious elephant against another.

sanskrit: sa saṃnipātas tumulo babhūvādbhutadarśanaḥ sātyakeś caiva śūrasya madrāṇām adhipasya ca yādṛśo vai purā vṛttaḥ śambarāmararājayoḥ
english: That tumultuous collision between the heroic Sātyaki and the lord of the Madras was a wondrous sight to behold, even such as once befell between Śambara and the king of the immortals.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ prekṣya samare madrarājaṃ vyavasthitam vivyādha daśabhir bāṇais tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Sātyaki, beholding the Madra king arrayed against him in battle, pierced him with ten arrows and cried, 'Stand, stand!'

sanskrit: madrarājas tu subhṛśaṃ viddhas tena mahātmanā sātyakiṃ prativivyādha citrapuṅkhaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And the Madra king, sorely wounded by that high-souled one, in turn pierced Sātyaki with sharp shafts of variegated feathering.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārthā maheṣvāsāḥ sātvatābhisṛtaṃ nṛpam abhyadravan rathais tūrṇaṃ mātulaṃ vadhakāmyayā
english: Then the sons of Pṛthā, those great archers, swiftly rushed in their chariots upon the king beset by the Sātvata—their uncle—eager to slay him.

sanskrit: tata āsīt parāmardas tumulaḥ śoṇitodakaḥ śūrāṇāṃ yudhyamānānāṃ siṃhānām iva nardatām
english: Then there arose a tumultuous clash, its waters of blood, among those battling heroes, like lions roaring in their rage.

sanskrit: teṣām āsīn mahārāja vyatikṣepaḥ parasparam siṃhānām āmiṣepsūnāṃ kūjatām iva saṃyuge
english: Their hurling of weapons against one another, O great king, was like the snarling of lions that crave the flesh of prey in the fray.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ bāṇasahasraughair ākīrṇā vasudhābhavat antarikṣaṃ ca sahasā bāṇabhūtam abhūt tadā
english: With the flooding thousands of their arrows the earth grew thickly strewn, and the very sky became, all at once, a thing made wholly of arrows.

sanskrit: śarāndhakāraṃ bahudhā kṛtaṃ tatra samantataḥ abhracchāyeva saṃjajñe śarair muktair mahātmabhiḥ
english: A darkness of arrows was wrought there manifoldly on every side; like the shadow of a cloud it gathered from the shafts loosed by those high-souled ones.

sanskrit: tatra rājañ śarair muktair nirmuktair iva pannagaiḥ svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ prakāśadbhir vyarocanta diśas tathā
english: There, O king, with the loosed arrows—golden-feathered and gleaming, like serpents sloughed of their skins—the quarters of the sky were made to shine.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutaṃ paraṃ cakre śalyaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ yad ekaḥ samare śūro yodhayām āsa vai bahūn
english: There Śalya, crusher of foes, performed a surpassing marvel, in that that hero alone fought against many in the battle.

sanskrit: madrarājabhujotsṛṣṭaiḥ kaṅkabarhiṇavājitaiḥ saṃpatadbhiḥ śarair ghorair avākīryata medinī
english: With the dreadful arrows let fly by the arm of the Madra king, fledged with heron and peacock feathers, raining down, the earth was overspread.

sanskrit: tatra śalyarathaṃ rājan vicarantaṃ mahāhave apaśyāma yathā pūrvaṃ śakrasyāsurasaṃkṣaye
english: There we beheld the chariot of Śalya, O king, ranging through that great battle, even as of old that of Śakra in the destruction of the Asuras.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ sainyās tava vibho madrarājapuraskṛtāḥ punar abhyadravan pārthān vegena mahatā raṇe
english: Saṃjaya said: Then your troops, O mighty lord, with the Madra king at their head, again rushed upon the sons of Pṛthā with great speed in the battle.

sanskrit: pīḍitās tāvakāḥ sarve pradhāvanto raṇotkaṭāḥ kṣaṇenaiva ca pārthāṃs te bahutvāt samaloḍayan
english: All your men, though hard pressed, charging on, frenzied for battle, in but a moment routed the sons of Pṛthā by their numbers.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ kurubhiḥ pāṇḍavā nāvatasthire nivāryamāṇā bhīmena paśyatoḥ kṛṣṇapārthayoḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas, cut down by the Kurus, could not hold their ground, though restrained by Bhīma, while Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha looked on.

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayaḥ kruddhaḥ kṛpaṃ saha padānugaiḥ avākirac charaugheṇa kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya in wrath overwhelmed Kṛpa, together with his foot-followers, and Kṛtavarman as well, with a flood of arrows.

sanskrit: śakuniṃ sahadevas tu sahasainyam avārayat nakulaḥ pārśvataḥ sthitvā madrarājam avaikṣata
english: Sahadeva held back Śakuni together with his host, while Nakula, standing at his side, kept his eye upon the Madra king.

sanskrit: draupadeyā narendrāṃś ca bhūyiṣṭhaṃ samavārayan droṇaputraṃ ca pāñcālyaḥ śikhaṇḍī samavārayat
english: The sons of Draupadī held back most of the kings, and Śikhaṇḍin the Pāñcāla held back the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu rājānaṃ gadāpāṇir avārayat śalyaṃ tu saha sainyena kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Bhīmasena, mace in hand, held back the king, while Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Kuntī held back Śalya together with his host.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ saṃsaktaṃ tatra tatra ha tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca saṃgrāmeṣv anivartinām
english: Then a battle close-locked arose, here and there, between your men and the foe, who never turned back from the fight.

sanskrit: tatra paśyāmahe karma śalyasyātimahad raṇe yad ekaḥ sarvasainyāni pāṇḍavānām ayudhyata
english: There we beheld the surpassingly mighty deed of Śalya in the battle, in that he alone fought against all the hosts of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: vyadṛśyata tadā śalyo yudhiṣṭhirasamīpataḥ raṇe candramaso 'bhyāśe śanaiścara iva grahaḥ
english: Śalya then appeared close beside Yudhiṣṭhira in the battle, like the planet Śanaiścara near the moon.

sanskrit: pīḍayitvā tu rājānaṃ śarair āśīviṣopamaiḥ abhyadhāvat punar bhīmaṃ śaravarṣair avākirat
english: Having afflicted the king with arrows like venomous serpents, he rushed again upon Bhīma and covered him with showers of shafts.

sanskrit: tasya tal lāghavaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathaiva ca kṛtāstratām apūjayann anīkāni pareṣāṃ tāvakāni ca
english: Beholding that lightness of his hand and his mastery of weapons, the ranks of both the foe and your own men honored him.

sanskrit: pīḍyamānās tu śalyena pāṇḍavā bhṛśavikṣatāḥ prādravanta raṇaṃ hitvā krośamāne yudhiṣṭhire
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, hard pressed by Śalya and sorely wounded, fled, abandoning the battle, while Yudhiṣṭhira cried out to them.

sanskrit: vadhyamāneṣv anīkeṣu madrarājena pāṇḍavaḥ amarṣavaśam āpanno dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tataḥ pauruṣam āsthāya madrarājam apīḍayat
english: As his ranks were being cut down by the Madra king, the Pāṇḍava Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Righteousness, gave way to indignation, and then, summoning his manhood, sorely pressed the Madra king.

sanskrit: jayo vāstu vadho veti kṛtabuddhir mahārathaḥ samāhūyābravīt sarvān bhrātṝn kṛṣṇaṃ ca mādhavam
english: Resolved in mind that it should be either victory or death, that mighty car-warrior summoned all his brothers and Kṛṣṇa the Mādhava, and spoke.

sanskrit: bhīṣmo droṇaś ca karṇaś ca ye cānye pṛthivīkṣitaḥ kauravārthe parākrāntāḥ saṃgrāme nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: Bhīṣma and Droṇa and Karṇa, and whatever other rulers of the earth strove for the cause of the Kauravas, have met their death in battle.

sanskrit: yathābhāgaṃ yathotsāhaṃ bhavantaḥ kṛtapauruṣāḥ bhāgo 'vaśiṣṭa eko 'yaṃ mama śalyo mahārathaḥ
english: Each according to his portion and his zeal, you have shown your manhood; one portion alone remains for me—Śalya, the mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: so 'ham adya yudhā jetum āśaṃse madrakeśvaram tatra yan mānasaṃ mahyaṃ tat sarvaṃ nigadāmi vaḥ
english: I therefore hope this day to conquer the lord of the Madrakas in combat; and all that is in my mind concerning this I now declare to you.

sanskrit: cakrarakṣāv imau śūrau mama mādravatīsutau ajeyau vāsavenāpi samare vīrasaṃmatau
english: Let these two heroes, the sons of Mādravatī, be the guards of my chariot-wheels—men unconquerable even by Vāsava in battle, honored among the brave.

sanskrit: sādhv imau mātulaṃ yuddhe kṣatradharmapuraskṛtau madarthaṃ pratiyudhyetāṃ mānārhau satyasaṃgarau
english: Worthily let these two, holding the warrior's law foremost, deserving of honor and true to their plighted word, fight against their uncle in battle for my sake.

sanskrit: māṃ vā śalyo raṇe hantā taṃ vāhaṃ bhadram astu vaḥ iti satyām imāṃ vāṇīṃ lokavīrā nibodhata
english: Either Śalya shall slay me in battle, or I shall slay him—good fortune be yours! Mark, O heroes of the world, this true word of mine.

sanskrit: yotsye 'haṃ mātulenādya kṣatradharmeṇa pārthivāḥ svayaṃ samabhisaṃdhāya vijayāyetarāya vā
english: This day, O princes, I myself, having so resolved, shall fight with my uncle by the law of the warrior—for victory or for the other.

sanskrit: tasya me 'bhyadhikaṃ śastraṃ sarvopakaraṇāni ca saṃyuñjantu raṇe kṣipraṃ śāstravad rathayojakāḥ
english: Let the yokers of chariots quickly furnish me, for this battle, with surpassing weaponry and all its appurtenances, according to the rule.

sanskrit: śaineyo dakṣiṇaṃ cakraṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnas tathottaram pṛṣṭhagopo bhavatv adya mama pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Let the grandson of Śini guard my right wheel and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the left, and let Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya be the guardian of my rear this day.

sanskrit: puraḥsaro mamādyāstu bhīmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ evam abhyadhikaḥ śalyād bhaviṣyāmi mahāmṛdhe
english: Let Bhīma, foremost of weapon-bearers, be my vanguard this day; thus shall I prove superior to Śalya in the great fray.

sanskrit: evam uktās tathā cakruḥ sarve rājñaḥ priyaiṣiṇaḥ tataḥ praharṣaḥ sainyānāṃ punar āsīt tadā nṛpa
english: Thus addressed, all those who sought the king's good did accordingly; and then, O king, joy arose once more among the troops.

sanskrit: pāñcālānāṃ somakānāṃ matsyānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ pratijñāṃ tāṃ ca saṃgrāme dharmarājasya pūrayan
english: Of the Pāñcālas, the Somakas, and the Matsyas especially, fulfilling that vow of the King of Righteousness in the battle—

sanskrit: tataḥ śaṅkhāṃś ca bherīś ca śataśaś caiva puṣkarān avādayanta pāñcālāḥ siṃhanādāṃś ca nedire
english: Then the Pāñcālas sounded conches and kettledrums and tabors by the hundred, and roared their lion-roars.

sanskrit: te 'bhyadhāvanta saṃrabdhā madrarājaṃ tarasvinaḥ mahatā harṣajenātha nādena kurupuṃgavāḥ
english: Enraged and swift, those bulls among the Kurus charged upon the Madra king with a great cry born of their gladness.

sanskrit: hrādena gajaghaṇṭānāṃ śaṅkhānāṃ ninadena ca tūryaśabdena mahatā nādayantaś ca medinīm
english: With the clangor of the bells of elephants, and with the blare of conches, and with the mighty din of trumpets, they made the earth resound.
